players.product: Sqale neutral-atom quantum computer (plus quantum clocks and RF sensors)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Kinsella: Q2 2026 revenue was a record $12.6 million, up 116% year-on-year, growth that was entirely organic and entirely from quantum, led by strong execution on QGG; CFO Ilan Hart: approximately 92% of Q2 revenue came from the U.S., up roughly 10 percentage points from the prior-year period, and the second-half outlook assumes a more normalized geographic mix.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 revenue $12.6 million (+116% YoY); ~92% from the U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Kinsella: Infleqtion is raising its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to approximately $43 million, driven by Q2 strength and increased visibility in the form of bookings across the board (the QGG contract among them); CFO Ilan Hart: the second half of 2026 is expected to be similar to the first half, with the same mix between sensing and compute and no real seasonality beyond contract award timing.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue outlook raised to approximately $43 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ilan Hart: RPO for Q2 2026 went up to $21 million, a slight increase from Q1 RPO.

CFO Ilan Hart: Q2 2026 GAAP loss from operations was $30.6 million versus $10.1 million in Q2 2025 and non-GAAP operating loss $17 million versus $7.3 million, with non-GAAP operating expenses up roughly $12 million year over year on headcount, technology development and public-company costs; cash generated from operations was $13.2 million including a temporary working-capital benefit of approximately $27 million (payroll taxes on option exercises, to be remitted in Q3), so operating cash burn excluding it was approximately $14 million; capex was $1.4 million, the 2026 outlook for a measured capex step-up (facility build-out) and a modest uptick in cash burn is unchanged; quarter-end cash, cash equivalents and available-for-sale securities were approximately $582 million with no debt.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP operating loss $30.6 million; non-GAAP operating loss $17 million; operating cash burn ~$14 million excluding ~$27 million benefit; capex $1.4 million; ~$582 million cash and securities, no debt

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Pranav Gokhale: Infleqtion remains on track to demonstrate 30 logical qubits on its Sqale quantum computer this year, and the logical qubit demonstrations will serve three end customers - one in finance, one in energy and one in precision medicine - all three revenue generating; CEO Matt Kinsella: remains confident of reaching the 30 logical qubit target this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 30 logical qubits targeted in 2026; 3 revenue-generating end customers

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Pranav Gokhale: Infleqtion achieved 2 logical qubits in 2024 and 12 logical qubits in 2025 on its Sqale quantum computer in Colorado (a 114-qubit system with 224 atom sites), via modular upgrades that retain 99% of the base system; to reach 30 logical qubits it tracks two characteristics, targeting atom loss per gate of less than about 2% during dynamic reconfiguration and a code rate of fewer than 10 physical qubits per logical qubit; it says it holds a commercial record for a 1,600-atom array and announced a new experimental record for dual-species two-qubit gate fidelity on its Sqale computer in Madison.
quarterly_data.figure: 2 logical qubits (2024); 12 logical qubits (2025); 114-qubit system, 224 sites; 1,600-atom array

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Pranav Gokhale: Infleqtion announced last month it is deploying a neutral-atom quantum computer integrated with NVIDIA NVQLink at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park, with delivery planned for 2027 and a new architecture designed to scale through modular upgrades to more than 50 logical qubits on the path to the system's 100 logical qubit goal; Infleqtion intends to make the system available over the cloud to a wide range of end customers.
quarterly_data.figure: delivery planned 2027; more than 50 logical qubits, 100 logical qubit goal

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Eaton: CTO Pranav Gokhale said Infleqtion announced a customer relationship with Eaton, which through private cloud access to Infleqtion's Sqale QPU, its Superstaq compiler and its quantum software is exploring how quantum computing can be applied to difficult energy problems.

U.S. Department of Energy: CEO Matt Kinsella said that in July the Department of Energy selected Infleqtion for three Genesis Mission projects across computing and sensing (spanning AI, nuclear applications and quantum sensing, per CTO Pranav Gokhale), bringing its computing and sensing capabilities together with government and commercial partners.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: selected Infleqtion for Genesis Mission projects

quarterly_data.signal: Customer National Quantum Computing Centre: CEO Matt Kinsella said Infleqtion recently delivered the United Kingdom's first and only operational 100 physical qubit quantum computer to the National Quantum Computing Centre; Infleqtion's teams have delivered quantum computers in the U.K. and Japan.

Partner Safran: CEO Matt Kinsella said the Safran relationship is a distribution agreement under which Infleqtion works with Safran to sell Tiqkers, plus a technology partnership embedding Safran's time-transfer technology into Tiqker (demonstrated with better than picosecond synchronization between Illinois and Indiana); CTO Pranav Gokhale said Tiqker is selling today, Safran is reaching global customers through its sales channels, Infleqtion secured a design win for satellite applications, and a next-generation Tiqker is planned to launch before the end of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: next-generation Tiqker launch planned before end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Customer NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory: CTO Pranav Gokhale said Infleqtion made progress with JPL on its Quantum Gravity Gradiometer pathfinder program, moving toward deployment of the first-ever quantum gravity sensor in orbit, with prototype testing being prepared at the Einstein Elevator in Germany; it has also started engaging potential customers for terrestrial uses such as critical mineral detection.

CTO Pranav Gokhale: Infleqtion introduced Quantum Spectrum, an RF sensing system detecting signals across a very wide frequency range in a compact system, with demand growing in defense applications and early commercial interest; its rapid context contract with the U.S. Navy uses its Contextual Machine Learning AI technology with current GPU hardware on large RF data sets, and it is advancing the same technology with additional customers including for the U.S. Army in GPS-denied environments and the European Space Agency.

Customer Aura Atomic: CFO Ilan Hart said Aura Atomic, a privately held neutral-atom quantum computing company, is a customer of Infleqtion's Quantum Cores business; during Q2 Infleqtion completed a strategic equity investment in it intended to support potential technical and commercial collaboration.

CEO Matt Kinsella: headcount has increased by just over 25% since the beginning of the year, mostly in technical roles, and Infleqtion is opening new quantum innovation facilities in Chicago, Oxford and Louisville with significantly expanded research, development and manufacturing capacity; in Colorado it has advanced plans to integrate its Sqale QPU with AI and classical HPC co-processing alongside its partnership with Oak Ridge National Laboratory's Quantum Science Center (CTO Pranav Gokhale).
quarterly_data.figure: headcount up just over 25% year to date

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Kinsella: Infleqtion currently provides a lot of private cloud access to various customers and intends to open up more over the public cloud in the not-too-distant future (CTO Pranav Gokhale: it is preparing all its machines for cloud access and expects markets for both on-premise system sales and cloud access for many years); recent market acceleration has improved visibility into 2027 revenue, with more detail expected at Q3, and Infleqtion is planning another measured increase in annual cash burn; long term it expects revenue to grow faster than operating costs; he said quantum computing is coming in a little hotter than he had expected, with strength in both sensing and computing.
